name: Luma
confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Gruber, James F. & Sigrid Lew. 2016. Interaction of pitch and phonation in Louma Oeshi. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 139: 2213 (abstract, 171st Meeting of the Acoustical Society of America). doi:10.1121/1.4950617
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Gruber, James F. & Sigrid Lew. 2016. Interaction of pitch and phonation in Louma Oeshi. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 139(4_Supplement): 2213. doi:10.1121/1.4950617
tone_statements.quote: This study focuses on the phonetic properties associated with Oeshi's three tones (high, mid, and low) and two registers (Tense, Lax), which fully intersect to yield a six-way suprasegmental contrast. … Our findings show a reliable three-way F0 contrast between tones and a single interaction with register such that High Tense words consistently fall (tones are otherwise level).
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low) crossed with two registers (Tense, Lax) giving a six-way contrast; High Tense words fall phonetically; acoustic study of 8 speakers; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Secondary; nothing on stress; lists Lew 2014, Gruber & Lew 2016, Lew 2023, Kingsada & Shintani 1999, Shintani et al. 2001 as the literature.

sources.citation: Lew, Sigrid. 2023. Notes on Luma, a Southern Ngwi language in Laos. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 16(2): xx-xxx (11 pp; placeholder roman pagination in the published PDF). Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press. CC-BY. hdl:10524/52518
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. §5 'Phonology and morphophonology' (p. xxvii, p. 8): 'Luma has three tones (High, Mid, Low) and two voice qualities. Modal voice occurs with all three tones, creaky voice only with Low and Mid tones. Tone sandhi is present in compounds'; consonant/vowel tables; tone change with tense on verbs noted but unanalysed. (eVols PDF bitstream could not be reached by automated download/direct download; full text obtained as markdown via the Jina reader proxy, page markers xx.xxx preserved.)

sources.citation: Lew, Sigrid & James Gruber. 2016. An acoustic analysis of tone and register in Louma Oeshi. Proceedings of the Linguistic Society of America 1, Article 33: 1-14. doi:10.3765/plsa.v1i0.3740
sources.note: No mention of stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: none). Instrumental study of the Eushi dialect: three level tones (High, Mid, Low) fully crossed with Lax/Tense register = six-way suprasegmental contrast; register 'behaves as a property of the syllable'; citation forms often carry a final glottal stop absent utterance-medially (§4, §5).

sources.citation: Lew, Sigrid. 2014. The phonetic realization of voice quality in Louma Uishui. Handout, 24th Annual Meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (SEALS 24), Yangon, 29 May 2014. 3 pp.
sources.note: No mention of stress. Phonation (lax vs constricted) in Louma Uishui; 11 vowels, one syllabic nasal, all syllables open; tense voice realised on onset, nucleus and/or coda. (Internet Archive copy 2024-11-05 of the jseals.org handout, live URL now 404.)
